# Wyrd — full machine-readable reference

Generated from the docs content tree and `crates/wyrd-spec/schemas/`. `architecture/wyrd-design.md` is the design authority; this schema dump may include implementation drift while `wyrd-spec` is reconciled.

## Home

- [Wyrd](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/): The typed control layer for AI systems: cards, a registry, and the Skald runtime.

## Overview

- [Overview](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/overview/): What Wyrd is, the coordination problem it solves, and what runs today.
- [Where Wyrd fits](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/overview/where-wyrd-fits/): Wyrd's position in the AI stack, the Mitari platform, the lifecycle loop, and what Wyrd is deliberately not.

## Get started

- [Get Started](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/get-started/): Install Wyrd from the repo and run the DataCard example end to end.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/tutorials/): Step-by-step walkthroughs from zero to your first registered card.
- [Your first card](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/tutorials/first-card/): Build a DataCard from a pandas DataFrame, save it to disk, and load it back — the one runnable card workflow today.

## Concepts

- [Concepts](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/): The Card/Spec/Run/Observation ontology — the four nouns everything else builds on.
- [Architecture](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/architecture/): The three products Wyrd ships from one source tree — control plane, runtime, and data plane — over one shared spec crate.
- [Audit Relay](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/audit-relay/): How Vala's background relay pumps audit events from the transactional outbox into the queryable Iceberg warehouse, with crash-safe idempotency and tenant isolation.
- [Authentication](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/authentication/): How Wyrd tokens work and how humans, API-key principals, and machine workloads each obtain one.
- [Authorization](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/authorization/): How Wyrd resolves permissions from token role claims, and how the PolicyHook authz extension gates the POST /v1/authz/check endpoint. Covers the request contract, hook context, and how to implement, register, and mesh-integrate a hook.
- [Card](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/card/): The typed, versioned envelope for one AI system component — its outer shape, lifecycle, and identity rules.
- [Card kinds](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/card-kinds/): The 16 native card kinds plus External, grouped by domain, with what each declares and its shipping status.
- [Cloud identity](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/cloud-identity/): Trusted OIDC issuers and workload bindings, with setup, admin CRUD, TOML seeding, and the sealing key.
- [Doctrine](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/doctrine/): The design doctrine behind Wyrd's nouns, layers, services, and public surfaces.
- [Identity and auth](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/concepts/identity-and-auth/): End-to-end map of how Wyrd scopes identity across tenants, users, services, agents, and workloads, and how the server verifies every request.

## How-to guides

- [How-to](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/): Goal-oriented recipes for declaring, evaluating, observing, and operating Wyrd components.
- [Build an Agent Workflow](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/build-a-workflow/): Author a workflow from Python, YAML, or Rust, then run and instrument it.
- [Build an Agent](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/build-an-agent/): Build a Wyrd Agent: prompt, tools, callbacks, session memory, and run config. Python and Rust side-by-side.
- [Declare](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/declare/): Author Wyrd cards in Python and save them locally — recipes for the three shipped kinds.
- [Declare a Data card](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/declare/data/): Author a DataCard from a pandas DataFrame and save it locally.
- [Declare a Model card](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/declare/model/): Author a ModelCard from a trained model and save it locally.
- [Declare a Prompt card](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/declare/prompt/): Author a PromptCard from a Prompt and save it locally.
- [Evaluate](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/evaluate/): Score agent runs and models against Wyrd eval definitions.
- [Observe](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/observe/): Read metrics, drift signals, and audit trails from card-governed components.
- [Operate](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/how-to/operate/): Run, restart, and manage card-governed components in production.

## Products and components

- [Products and components](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/products/): Choose the Wyrd product or subsystem you are learning, building with, or maintaining.

## Skald runtime

- [Skald](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/skald/): The Wyrd runtime for provider clients, prompts, tools, agents, and workflows.

## Bifrost

- [Bifrost](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/): The Wyrd analytical warehouse. Apache Iceberg tables, DataFusion queries, and a typed read surface for all Vala observations.
- [Architecture](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/architecture/): Component responsibilities, data flow, storage model, concurrency, durability, and scaling for Gate, Scribe, Oracle, and Forge.
- [Data plane internals](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/data-plane-internals/): Scribe WAL format, seal state machine, vala.file_list schema, Forge maintenance, and audit chain sealing.
- [Forge system overview](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/forge/): How Forge maintains Bifrost data and connects Gate, Scribe, Oracle, Iceberg, Postgres, and object storage.
- [Quickstart](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/quickstart/): Emit an observation via vala-sdk and query it back through a typed ValaQueryService method.
- [Reading Data](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/reading-data/): ValaQueryService typed methods, signed page tokens, payload-read permissions, the governed generic SQL surface, and Arrow conversion.
- [Schema](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/schema/): Pre-declared Bifrost domain tables, physical schemas, system columns, and type mapping.
- [SLOs](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/slos/): Bifrost performance targets and methodology, including Forge maintenance benchmarks.
- [Writing Data](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/bifrost/writing-data/): vala-sdk producer, batching, backpressure, payload governance, and tenant stamping.

## Cards

- [Cards overview](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/): The card envelope, how registration works, and a catalog of every card kind with its status.
- [Data](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/data/): Generated reference for the Wyrd Data card spec.
- [Model](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/model/): Generated reference for the Wyrd Model card spec.
- [Prompt](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/prompt/): Generated reference for the Wyrd Prompt card spec.

## API reference

- [API reference](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/api/): Error catalog, OpenAPI summary, and JSON Schema inventory — all generated from source.
- [Errors](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/api/errors/): Error handling guidance for Wyrd API clients and agents.
- [OpenAPI](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/api/openapi/): Generated summary of the Wyrd OpenAPI contract.
- [Schemas](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/api/schemas/): Generated inventory of Wyrd JSON Schemas.

## Reference

- [Reference](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/reference/): The literal contract — CLI verbs, card schemas, error codes, and the API surface.
- [CLI](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/reference/cli/): The wyrd binary — auth, eval, and principal commands, with every flag and environment variable.

## Self-hosting

- [Self-hosting](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/): Run the Wyrd server yourself. Configuration, database, storage, auth, and the runtime architecture.
- [Architecture](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/architecture/): The server's components, how a request flows through the protective edge, and how the process supervises and shuts down.
- [Authentication](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/authentication/): The principals, tokens, and grants the server uses, plus generating and mounting the signing and sealing keys.
- [Binary](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/binary/): Deploy the compiled server to a host or VM.
- [Configuration](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/configuration/): Every environment variable, the config file resolution order, and the validation rules the server enforces at boot.
- [Database](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/database/): Postgres setup for the server. External and embedded modes, the roles the server needs, and migrations.
- [Docker](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/docker/): Run the open-source server image against your own Postgres and object storage.
- [Enterprise](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/enterprise/): Multi-tenant SaaS deployment with custom policy, audit, and identity.
- [Local development](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/local-development/): Run the server on your machine with embedded Postgres, local storage, and a development signing key.
- [Running the server](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/running-the-server/): The CLI, serve modes, the boot sequence, graceful shutdown, and the health and readiness probes.
- [SSO and OIDC](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/sso-and-oidc/): Wire an identity provider for human single sign-on and for machine workload federation.
- [Storage](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/self-hosting/storage/): The artifact store. Local, S3, GCS, and Azure backends with the credentials each one needs.

## For Agents

- [For Agents](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/for-agents/): Machine-readable surface, stable API paths, and the rules agents must follow when reading and updating Wyrd.
- [Error remediation](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/for-agents/error-remediation/): How agents should handle Wyrd errors.
- [Agent workflow](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/for-agents/workflow/): A copyable end-to-end workflow for agents that declare cards and register them over HTTP.

## Fathom

- [Fathom](https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/fathom/): The enterprise intelligence layer that reads Wyrd's typed model and turns behavior into evidence. Coming soon.

## Card schemas

### AgentCard

Declare an agent that Wyrd can describe, govern, evaluate, install references for, and observe. Execution stays in the user or framework runtime.

URL: https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/
Schema source: crates/wyrd-spec/schemas/agent_spec.json

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "definitions": {
    "AgentRunConfigSpec": {
      "description": "Pure-serde mirror of the Skald agent run configuration.",
      "properties": {
        "max_iterations": {
          "description": "Maximum loop iterations before the agent stops.",
          "format": "uint32",
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "type": [
            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "session_recent_limit": {
          "description": "Maximum recent session turns loaded at run start.",
          "format": "uint",
          "minimum": 0.0,

            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
        "timeout_ms": {
          "description": "Overall agent run timeout in milliseconds.",
          "format": "uint64",
          "minimum": 0.0,

            "integer",
            "null"
          ]
        },
```

### DriftCard

Describe the drift contract Wyrd uses to watch behavior over time.

URL: https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/
Schema source: crates/wyrd-spec/schemas/drift_spec.json


### EvalCard

Define an evaluation suite, scoring rule, or acceptance check.

URL: https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/
Schema source: crates/wyrd-spec/schemas/eval_spec.json

### ExperimentCard

Group work-in-progress runs and candidate changes under a single intent.

URL: https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/
Schema source: crates/wyrd-spec/schemas/experiment_spec.json

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
```

### WorkflowCard

Describe a coordinated sequence of operators, tools, agents, or services.

URL: https://mitari-ai.github.io/wyrd/cards/
